name: TX-29
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Sylvia Garcia running with a large fundraising edge
Republican challenger has raised essentially no money
Prediction markets price Garcia near certain to win
model.rationale: Garcia holds a D+17 district with incumbency advantages and roughly a million dollars raised plus outside support, while Fierro has shown no fundraising footprint. Markets price Garcia at about 97%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending intervention for the Republican challenger, which has shown no signs of materializing, is the main thing that could move this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sylvia Garcia seeks another term in a Houston-area district that leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about 17 points. She enters the general election as a well-established incumbent who easily secured renomination. Her Republican opponent, Martha Fierro, has reported essentially no fundraising and no outside support, leaving her with few visible resources to compete.

Garcia has raised nearly a million dollars and benefits from over half a million dollars in outside spending on her behalf. Prediction markets put her chances near certain, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the outlook rests on the district's fundamentals, which point to a comfortable incumbent win.
